title: Q-RES-perez-lopez-1974-P4: Repeating actions whose side effects keep growing (measured 0.842, target >= 0.9)
body:
**Owner:** product-manager
**Trigger:** research pass: perez-lopez-1974 finding P4 is not-met (measured 0.842)
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation research --probe perez-lopez-1974:P4
**Prediction:** action_classes_consistent_share >= 0.9 within 336 h
**Out of scope:** editing the study, its target or the paper to match the code; the measurement is changed only by changing the mechanism
**Closing probe:** `python3 -m foundation research --probe perez-lopez-1974:P4`
**Status:** open

Concern: Repeating actions whose side effects keep growing. The study: "An ultrastable system is one that has a built-in mechanism which ensures consistency, that is to say, a mechanism which systematically discards action alternatives that have been found to have decreasing efficiency after they were tried."

Mechanisms that should answer it: FREELY-ADAPTIVE-1 (foundation/freeadapt.py); ULTRASTABILITY-1 (foundation/ultrastability.py).

Metric: share of judged action classes whose recent actions mostly left the other essential variables inside their limits (foundation/freeadapt.py), target >= 0.9. Improve the mechanism (or add one) until the probe passes; the white paper at /research updates itself from the same measurement.
